strategy.summary: Reproduce issue 16497 by building astropy from source at buggy commit ed0072408b14 and running the developer's regression test test_regression_16497_nan_treatment_consistency in astropy/convolution/tests/test_convolve.py. On the buggy revision the NaN-free boundary='fill' call with fill_value=nan produces NaN edge values, so the finiteness assertion fails. On the fixed revision the edge NaNs are interpolated away and every assertion passes. Versions come from the issue's Versions block, since the evidence documents no constraints.

system_packages: gcc (C compiler able to build astropy's Cython/C extensions)
build_commands: pip install numpy==1.26.4 scipy==1.13.0 matplotlib==3.8.4 pyerfa==2.0.1.4 pytest cython extension-helpers setuptools_scm
pinned_because: numpy 1.26.4 is taken from the issue 16497 Versions block as the reproduction environment; no documented constraint or era table entry exists, so this is a choice, not a requirement
scipy 1.13.0 and matplotlib 3.8.4 are also from the issue Versions block and are not numerically relevant to convolve
pyerfa 2.0.1.4 is from the issue Versions block and is not numerically relevant
astropy is built from source at the buggy commit rather than taken as the 6.1.0 release from pip install astropy, because the defect lives in the source revision and the wheel would not match it

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy ed0072408b14 the test FAILS: with ar=np.ones((10,10)) and Gaussian2DKernel(1,x_size=5,y_size=5), convolve(boundary='fill', fill_value=np.nan, preserve_nan=True) returns NaN edge values, so np.all(np.isfinite(result_convolve)) is False and the test fails there (or earlier at assert_array_almost_equal against convolve_fft). On the fixed revision (nan_interpolate also set when boundary=='fill' and np.isnan(fill_value)) the test PASSES: the NaN-free result is finite, matches convolve_fft to decimal=10, and with ar[5,5]=nan exactly one NaN appears at [5,5] in both outputs.
strategy.numerical_probe: Run convolve on np.ones((10,10)) with Gaussian2DKernel(1, x_size=5, y_size=5), boundary='fill', fill_value=np.nan, preserve_nan=True, and count np.isnan in the result. Buggy: nonzero count equal to the edge buffer. Fixed: zero. Repeat with boundary=None to see zero bleed from the edge.

input_output_examples.input: astropy.convolution.convolve applied to ar = np.ones((10, 10)) with no NaN values
input_output_examples.buggy_output: result contains a NaN buffer of kernel_size//2 at the edges
input_output_examples.expected_output: no NaN buffer of kernel_size//2 at the edges; result matches convolve_fft and does not depend on whether NaNs are present

risks: Needs a source build at ed0072408b14: the wheel from pip install astropy is a released version and will not reproduce the defect, and the C extensions must compile against numpy 1.26.4.
The fix is from a WIP PR and the diff is partial, so ed0072408b14 must be the true parent of the fix; confirm the fixed revision matches the nan_interpolate change before trusting the transition.
Expected all-NaN output for convolve versus zeros for convolve_fft (issue 11920) is disputed; the regression test does not depend on that all-NaN case, but a different test selection could.

The test body is truncated in the passages; the kernel arguments beyond Gaussian2DKernel(1, x_size=5, y_size=5) are only partly visible, so the test should be run from the actual file at the fixed commit.
No dtype is stated (null), so the test is run at the default float64 with ones input; float32 behaviour is unverified.

No platform, architecture, sanitizer, or threading requirement is stated in the evidence, so none is assumed; if the defect only appears under a specific platform the transition may not reproduce elsewhere.

Versions numpy 1.26.4 and astropy 6.1.0 are from the issue reporter's environment and are not documented constraints for this revision; a different numpy major could change edge behaviour and is not tested here.

oracle.tolerance: assert_array_almost_equal decimal=10 between convolve and convolve_fft, plus exact isfinite and NaN-count checks
oracle.reference_source: convolve_fft output in the same test
oracle.why: The developer test compares convolve against convolve_fft to decimal=10 and checks NaN counts exactly; the transition is decided by these assertions.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On ed0072408b14 the NaN-free convolve result contains NaN edge values, so np.all(np.isfinite(result_convolve)) is False and the assertion fails, or the earlier assert_array_almost_equal against convolve_fft fails first.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With nan_interpolate also set for boundary='fill' and np.isnan(fill_value), the edge NaNs are interpolated, all finiteness and NaN-count assertions hold, and the convolve and convolve_fft outputs agree to decimal=10.
